entry_state._derivation: DERIVED 2026-09-20: a book's entry state is the preceding book's exit state. B0N entry = B0N-1 exit, so this cites BB05's exit_state_locks rather than restating them - one source, not two. Structural coordinates only; the grid holds the descriptions. Inherits status `proposed` from those grid rows. Regenerate rather than hand-edit. Ledger section 60.
entry_state._status: proposed - inherited from the grid rows
entry_state.world: DERIVED: the world as B05 leaves it. See book_context_B05.json exit_state_locks: M17, M18, M19.
entry_state.key_character_states: DERIVED: as B05 leaves them. Character-level state is not carried in the milestone grid, which records events rather than per-character condition. What IS derivable is cited above; per-character detail needs either a character-arc layer (none exists yet - CLAUDE.md section 8.0 lists character arcs as genuinely unstructured) or an author pass. Not invented here.

Ledger section 59.
exit_state_locks._status: proposed - inherited from the grid rows

escalation_permissions.derivation: Union of the three act bands beneath this book (S1.T2.B06.A1/.A2/.A3): min of mins, max of maxes, per axis. No judgement was applied to any value. Regenerate rather than hand-edit: if an act band changes, this block is stale.
escalation_permissions.source: act_overlays/ rolled up 2026-09-20; the act values themselves come from proposals/concord-2026/ENVELOPE_INTERIM_VALUES_V2_2026-09-19.md
escalation_permissions.superseded_finding: CLOSED 2026-09-20. This field recorded that the book's derived band exceeded its trilogy container. The trilogy containers are now DERIVED from the books beneath them by the same rollup, so a book cannot exceed a container computed from itself and the breach no longer exists. Ledger section 57. TWO CORRECTIONS to what this field said: (1) it called the trilogy scalars "older author-set ceilings that were never reconciled". They were not. All three trilogy files carried identical W3/U5 beside an unfilled TODO reading "Populate trilogy-specific ceilings and exceptions" - SKELETON DEFAULTS, never populated. Same class of misattribution as the two CLAUDE.md errors in ledger section 52. (2) it counted fx as a breached axis. There is no trilogy fx_max; `default_vfx_ceiling` is a DEFAULT, and exceeding a default is not a breach.

continuity_hooks._derivation: DERIVED 2026-09-20 from grids/milestones_payoffs.csv `required_setups`, which encodes 54 dependency edges, 33 of them cross-book, with zero dangling and zero backward references. A cross-book dependency IS a continuity hook. Regenerate rather than hand-edit: if the grid changes, this block is stale. Milestone IDs are cited rather than described - the grid holds the descriptions, and duplicating them here would create a second copy to drift. Ledger section 59.
